rule: When creating a dated note from a session, extract and record each atomic fact as its own short statement that includes any explicit numeric values, proper names, or dates mentioned (e.g., counts, miles, purchase items, hostel name, person named) and keep the original date of the session with that statement.
rationale: Many failures came from missing concrete facts (a coin added, hostel name, advisor name). Capturing atomic facts with their numeric values/names and the session date ensures later stages can find exact facts instead of answering 'I don't know.'

rule: Record user preferences, experiences, and stated affinities exactly as given (brief paraphrase or quoted phrase) and do not add inferred context or extra specifics beyond what the user said.
rationale: Answers that added unsupported personal details (extra experiences, invented travel dates, additional items) harmed accuracy. Storing only what was actually stated prevents downstream hallucination.

rule: When merging dated notes, do not invent or infer new numeric values, dates, or item details; compute aggregate totals (sums, counts, total distance) only if every contributing dated note explicitly provides the necessary numeric value—otherwise mark the aggregate as unknown and list the source notes used.
rationale: Incorrect totals and invented specifics caused several failures. This rule forces aggregates to be provable from the map notes and prevents the pack from asserting unsupported counts or dates.

rule: When a session mentions a named person or organization in connection with a specific role, title, recommendation, or fact (e.g., 'President's Chief Advisor for Science and Technology: Dr. X', a recommended hostel name, or 'manager Rachel led team Y'), extract and record an atomic dated statement that links the name and the role/title/recommendation and cite the source/session date.
rationale: Failures show the reducer claims 'no record' of explicit person-title links and specific recommendations. R1 demands extraction of proper names but does not require recording explicit person↔role or recommendation pairings; this map rule ensures role/title/recommendation facts are captured as distinct atomic notes so downstream merge/answers can retrieve them.

rule: When merging dated numeric statements about the same item/category, preserve all original dated numeric statements and, if at least one numeric value exists, compute and include an explicit aggregated value (sum or count) labeled as 'computed from' with the list of contributing dated notes; if some relevant notes lack numeric values, mark which source notes lacked numbers rather than treating the aggregate as wholly unknown.
rationale: Current rule R3 is too conservative and led to answers that claimed 'unknown' or produced incorrect counts. Keeping all source numeric statements and exposing a computed aggregate with provenance avoids dropping valid numerical facts and makes it clear when some notes are missing numeric data.

rule: When creating dated notes, extract and record every explicit enumerated or countable item and every explicit named recommendation or role as its own atomic statement (e.g., inventory counts, team member counts, counts of items, named hostel/hotel recommendations, named persons with titles), preserving exact numeric values, exact names, and the original session date.
rationale: Failures show that numeric counts, roster sizes, named recommendations, and titled persons were not captured into the pack. This rule forces the map stage to capture any explicit counts, enumerations, and named recommendations/titles so those facts are available later for answering direct factual queries.

rule: When merging dated notes about the same factual subject (same inventory, same person/title, same recommended place), keep all distinct dated statements but select the single most recent explicit statement as the canonical fact for quick answers; when multiple numeric statements exist, do not average—use the latest numeric value and record its source date.
rationale: Pack-level answers must reflect the latest explicit facts rather than omit or average them. Several failures came from missing or wrong counts and names because the merge step dropped or obscured the most recent explicit statement. This rule keeps historical entries while ensuring the canonical value used for answers is the most recent explicit one.

rule: When creating a dated note, record every explicit named entity and title (people, organizations, place names, product/hostel/hotel names) and every explicit factual assertion (e.g., counts, dates, job titles, named roles) verbatim as separate atomic statements, even if they occur only once or seem incidental.
rationale: Training failures show specific named facts (person names, hostel names, job titles) and explicit counts were missing from the compiled pack. Ensuring every explicit named entity and factual assertion is captured as its own atomic statement prevents one-off but important facts from being dropped at the map stage.

rule: When merging map notes into the final pack, preserve all unique atomic factual statements (including numeric counts and named entities) from the map stage; if budget constraints require removal, preferentially keep atomic factual statements and drop or compress subjective, ambiguous, or conversational material instead.
rationale: The model omitted concrete facts and counts in the final pack, causing incorrect 'I don't know' answers. This rule ensures that verifiable facts and numbers survive the reduce stage, and that any trimming favors removing non-factual content rather than dropping explicit facts.
